V.rationale: Visa exhibits excellent fundamental health and trajectory: Q2 FY2026 revenue of $11.23B grew 17% YoY (strongest since 2022), net income of $6.02B with 51.7% net margin and 62.4% ROE, operating margin of 61.1%. Revenue has grown sequentially for 5 quarters ($9.51B → $11.23B). The business is asset-light with near-zero marginal transaction costs, creating a durable competitive moat through network effects (4.5B+ cards, 175M+ merchants). Value-added services grew 27% YoY to 30% of revenue, diversifying beyond core transaction processing. Balance sheet is strong with $35.7B equity and manageable leverage. Operating cash flow of $3.01B in Q2 (seasonally lower than Q1's $6.78B) remains robust. The company authorized a $20B buyback and raised full-year guidance, signaling management confidence. On valuation, the stock at $322.52 is down ~14% from its 52-week high of $375.51, trading at ~25x earnings per news reports — below its five-year average. The recent pullback reflects regulatory overhang (Credit Card Competition Act) rather than fundamental deterioration. Near-term catalyst: the Q2 earnings beat (EPS $3.31 vs $3.10 consensus, revenue $11.23B vs $10.75B consensus) reported April 28, combined with the $20B buyback authorization, provides a credible re-rating path as the market digests the acceleration from 15% to 17% revenue growth. Risks include regulatory headwinds on interchange fees and rising rates (10Y at 4.47%), but these are well-flagged and the legislative amendment has repeatedly failed to attach to legislation.
